title: DDCA to Review DPL Selection Rules After Dev Chaudhary Controversy Exposes Loopholes
excerpt: The controversial selection of little-known cricketer Dev Chaudhary by New Delhi Tigers has put the Delhi Premier League's player-selection process under intense scrutiny, prompting promises of rule changes.
body:
• Dev Chaudhary, a 22-year-old with minimal senior cricket credentials, was selected by New Delhi Tigers through a DPL rule allowing franchises to pick three players outside the auction.
  • Chaudhary scored 0 off 2 balls and 16 off 24 balls in his two DPL appearances, drawing widespread social media criticism for his unusual batting stance and fielding.
  • DDCA Apex Council member Shyam Sharma called the rule "an absolute shame" and confirmed the body will review it after the tournament concludes.
  • New Delhi Tigers, coached by Virat Kohli's childhood coach Rajkumar Sharma, sit last among eight teams with just one win from ten matches.

The Controversial Clause Under Scrutiny

The Delhi & Districts Cricket Association (DDCA) is facing mounting pressure to overhaul the Delhi Premier League's player-selection regulations after the inclusion of Dev Chaudhary by the New Delhi Tigers sparked a firestorm of criticism across Indian cricket circles.

At the heart of the controversy lies a DPL rule that permits each franchise to select up to three players outside the main auction, provided those players have appeared in at least five DDCA League matches. Several DDCA Apex Council members had opposed the clause before it was approved, warning it could open the door to nepotism and the selection of undeserving players.

"It has been an absolute shame. I was the first one who had raised my voice about this rule. They made a criteria that five DDCA League games would be enough to qualify for a place in DPL without auction."

— Shyam Sharma, DDCA Apex Council member

Sharma told PTI he had raised concerns about the rule on the forum, asking what would happen if a player who had not performed was still picked. "Dev Chaudhary has been exposed but there are many players like this who have come into the teams on recommendations," he said.

Chaudhary's On-Field Performance

Chaudhary played two matches as an opener for New Delhi Tigers during the DPL 2026 season. In his debut on August 16 against South Delhi Superstarz, he was dismissed for a duck off just two deliveries. His second outing on August 19 against West Delhi Lions produced 16 runs off 24 balls—an innings that went viral for all the wrong reasons.

Videos of his unusual batting stance, unconventional grip, and inability to hit a single powerful shot circulated widely on social media. He also played five consecutive dot balls against a spinner during the Powerplay, leaving commentators and former players baffled at his presence in the playing XI. Additional footage of Chaudhary struggling during fielding drills further fueled the backlash.

The New Delhi Tigers eventually dropped Chaudhary from their playing XI for the 39th match against South Delhi Superstarz on August 24.

Questions Over Background and Credentials

Chaudhary's cricketing background has come under particular scrutiny. A 2021 DDCA Under-19 preliminary trial document listed him as an all-rounder focusing on middle-order batting and right-arm fast bowling—a profile critics say does not match the demands of opening the batting in a high-profile T20 league.

Social media users labeled his selection a "fraud," with some alleging "political or wealthy-family backing." One widely shared post described him as "the son of a big businessman in Delhi," noting that "so many genuinely talented players go to waste."

Chaudhary himself has pushed back. He clarified that he represented Sporting Club in the DDCA T20 League in 2025, playing seven matches and scoring 56 runs, which he said made him eligible for the DPL player auction. He also noted that he is coached by Rajkumar Sharma, widely known as Virat Kohli's childhood coach, who heads the New Delhi Tigers.

What Happens Next

DDCA Secretary Ashok Sharma confirmed the controversial rule will be examined once the tournament concludes. DDCA President Rohan Jaitley, whose association launched the DPL, is expected to initiate a comprehensive review of the out-of-auction selection clause.

The New Delhi Tigers have endured a dismal season regardless of the Chaudhary controversy, sitting last among the eight-team table with just one victory from ten matches. For the DPL to maintain credibility as Delhi's premier domestic T20 competition, the DDCA faces clear pressure to tighten selection criteria and ensure transparency in future editions.
